caption: Fig. 1. Representative acquisition conditions and reference FDI annotations. Panoramic radiographs, smartphone intraoral photographs, and DSLR photographs are shown with their existing bounding-box annotations. The examples illustrate differences in global field of view, tooth scale, framing, and illumination. Visible spaces alone do not establish clinically missing teeth.

Fig. 2. DENT-STRIDE component family. The domain settings in Table 2 determine which components are active: CMFA for Mobile/DSLR, HOOA for Mobile, identity supervision for Mobile/Pano, factor-score fusion for Mobile, and SpatialShape for Pano. Other refiners are supplementary comparisons. Prediction and factor heads branch from decoded query features; the prototype bank supplies training supervision only. The lower panel shows parallel native loss terms combined before optimization; configuration-dependent auxiliary terms are defined in Section 3.5.

Fig. 3. Training-derived center templates for the 32 permanent DENTEX FDI classes. Each panel shows the class-specific center distribution in normalized image coordinates, based on training-box means and full regularized covariances. The templates are fixed at inference and are separate from the learnable appearance prototypes; shape statistics are provided in Supplementary Fig. S4.

Fig. 4. CMFA: cross-gated adjacent-scale exchange followed by spatial gating. The lower panels identify its four insertion sites and summarize the operations. CMFA is active in the selected Mobile and DSLR configurations, but not in Pano.

Fig. 5. HOOA refinement in the Mobile configuration. The local branch L interacts with sigmoid-gated context to form O₂; a high-pass branch provides E. Concatenated responses are projected and gated before the bounded residual update. DW denotes depthwise convolution, σ sigmoid, ⊙ element-wise product, and ⊕ addition. The separate CEDv2 comparison architecture is shown in Supplementary Fig. S1.

Fig. 6. Controlled module and resolution comparisons. (A) Mobile at 1024: base, feature processing, structured identity, and their combination. (B) Mobile at 640. (C) Pano auxiliary supervision with factor inference fusion and geometric scoring disabled. (D) DSLR CMFA × optimizer comparison. Open symbols are the actual seeds; diamonds and bars are mean ± sample SD (n = 3). Thin lines connect corresponding base and combined-model seeds. Panels A/B use the same AP range; other domain ranges differ.

Fig. 7. DSLR accuracy versus model size, with a compact-model enlargement. Model names are attached to the points; RT-DETR-L is retained. Error bars show sample SD across seeds 0, 1, and 2 for the controlled reference, DENT-STRIDE-DSLR, CMFA + AdamW, Official DEIM-s, and RT-DETRv2-S. Remaining comparators retain single-seed values without error bars. No Pareto-frontier connector is imposed. Input and training differences follow the framework protocols described in Section 4.6.

Fig. 8. Mobile inter-module comparison using independently trained controlled seed-0 models at the same resolution and operating threshold. Columns show the original image, reference annotations, baseline, features only, identity only, and complete configuration; each case pairs the whole image with an identical local enlargement. Features comprise CMFA and HOOA; identity comprises factorized supervision/fusion and prototype auxiliary supervision. FDI text labels identify the highlighted target’s localization match, while other retained predictions remain visible as boxes. Complete validation results, rather than these selected examples, establish each configuration’s measured performance.

Fig. 9. Four-way Pano prior replay at identical weights. (A) COCO AP and (B) AR100. Each line connects one of the three checkpoints across no prior, center-only, shape-only, and combined scoring; filled diamonds and bars show mean ± sample SD. Scores are recomputed before native top-k selection. Factor inference fusion is disabled in all four settings.

Fig. 10. Same-checkpoint DENTEX anatomical-prior replay. Each column starts from the same 300 pre-top-k query boxes and logits; only the training-derived center/shape score terms change before native top-k selection. Rows compare reference annotations with no prior, center only, shape only, and combined scoring using score ≥0.30; all local enlargements share the same region. (A) combined scoring suppresses incorrect/repeated candidates, reducing false-positive predictions from 9 to 6 while retaining 27 correct matches; the highlighted FDI 12 tooth is retained and an additional FDI 13 candidate falls below the display threshold. This is score-based candidate suppression, not a corrected highest-class identity. (B) the same highlighted query box changes its highest retained label from the correct FDI 27 to FDI 28; image-level correct matches decrease from 15 to 14. Bounding boxes are unchanged. These selected examples illustrate both favourable and adverse scoring effects.

Fig. 11. Internal sensitivity of CMFA gates, factor supervision, prototype number, and DualOpt operations. Positive ΔAP means that the displayed alternative exceeds the stated group reference; it is not an improvement attributed to the intact module. Factor supervision uses fusion off in both phases. DualOpt controls retain ordinary AdamW base decay. All points are seed 0, without uncertainty bars; — has no numeric mark. Supplementary Fig. S6 provides HOOA, temperature, background-loss, and fusion panels.

Fig. 12A. Same-image smartphone validation comparison. Columns show the original image, reference annotations, controlled baseline, RT-DETR-L, and DENT-STRIDE; each enlarged row uses an identical target region across columns. Teal boxes denote reference annotations and orange boxes denote model predictions. Saved seed-0 model outputs use score ≥0.30 and clinical FDI decoding; FDI text labels identify the highlighted target’s localization match, while other retained predictions remain visible as boxes. (A) the highlighted reference tooth is FDI 51; the controlled baseline wrong assignment (11) and full-model correct assignment (51) accompany image-level correct-match counts of 4 and 7. (B) the highlighted reference tooth is FDI 62; the controlled baseline correct assignment (62) and full-model wrong assignment (52) accompany image-level correct-match counts of 5 and 2. Examples include an improvement and a deterioration and do not estimate their population frequencies. The external detector retains its framework-specific training and post-processing.

Fig. 12B. Same-image panoramic validation comparison. Columns show the original image, reference annotations, controlled baseline, RT-DETR-L, and DENT-STRIDE; each enlarged row uses an identical target region across columns. Teal boxes denote reference annotations and orange boxes denote model predictions. Saved seed-0 model outputs use score ≥0.30 and clinical FDI decoding; FDI text labels identify the highlighted target’s localization match, while other retained predictions remain visible as boxes. (A) the highlighted reference tooth is FDI 28; the controlled baseline wrong assignment (27) and full-model correct assignment (28) accompany image-level correct-match counts of 26 and 29. (B) the highlighted reference tooth is FDI 28; the controlled baseline correct assignment (28) and full-model wrong assignment (27) accompany image-level correct-match counts of 29 and 28. Examples include an improvement and a deterioration and do not estimate their population frequencies. The external detector retains its framework-specific training and post-processing.

Fig. 12C. Same-image DSLR validation comparison. Columns show the original image, reference annotations, controlled baseline, RT-DETR-L, and DENT-STRIDE; each enlarged row uses an identical target region across columns. Teal boxes denote reference annotations and orange boxes denote model predictions. Saved seed-0 model outputs use score ≥0.30 and clinical FDI decoding; FDI text labels identify the highlighted target’s localization match, while other retained predictions remain visible as boxes. (A) the highlighted reference tooth is FDI 52; the controlled baseline wrong assignment (53) and full-model correct assignment (52) accompany image-level correct-match counts of 9 and 13. (B) the highlighted reference tooth is FDI 64; the controlled baseline correct assignment (64) and full-model wrong assignment (24) accompany image-level correct-match counts of 22 and 20. Examples include an improvement and a deterioration and do not estimate their population frequencies. The external detector retains its framework-specific training and post-processing.

Fig. 13. Prototype diagnostics from the seed-0 Mobile EMA checkpoint used in the qualitative comparison. (A) Cosine similarity between normalized class-centroid prototypes, with classes ordered by FDI quadrant Q1–Q8. Grey unsupported slots correspond to 18, 28, 38, and 48. (B) Each open point is a supported FDI class and the short bar is the mean within its quadrant; cohesion is mean pairwise cosine similarity among four normalized prototypes. The bank is training-only supervision. Per-class cohesion is supplied in Supplementary Fig. S8.

Fig. 14. Auxiliary quadrant, position, and dentition predictions for 2,335 localized unique ordinary queries from the same Mobile seed-0 checkpoint. Rows are reference factors and columns are predictions; colours and annotations show row-normalized percentages. Grey rows with a dash have no reference observations. Quadrants retain the FDI first digit, position uses the second digit, and dentition is primary/permanent. These are structured identity heads, not objectness heads. The unique-query capture protocol differs from the native post-top-k detection endpoints.

Fig. 15. Actual Mobile forward-pass responses for the improvement example in Fig. 12A. The first row shows the image, CMFA channel gates gA/gB, and its spatial gate Gs; the second shows HOOA local, context, high-pass, and consumed second-order responses; the third shows HOOA channel/spatial gates and its input/output. Channel gates are arranged as 16 × 16 channel grids. Gates retain raw [0,1] values; response RMS maps are independently scaled by their 99th percentile and clipped to [0,1]. The maps are not Grad-CAM or a causal test of AP improvement.

Fig. S1. CEDv2 comparison architecture. Guided top-down and bottom-up operations refine the projected pyramid before the main encoder. CEDv2 is inactive in the domain-configured models. ↑ denotes resizing/upsampling except the labelled learned stride-2 operation; C denotes concatenation, σ sigmoid, and ⊙ element-wise multiplication.

Fig. S2. SMWG, an optional Fourier spectral-modulation and fine-to-coarse detail-guidance refiner. This evaluated implementation uses rFFT2/irFFT2 with radial frequency-band masks; it does not perform a discrete wavelet decomposition.

Fig. S3. MPF and UCM per-level comparison refiners. MPF mixes local, channel-reweighting, and context paths; UCM uses local mean/variance to interpolate detail and context updates. MPF precedes UCM when both are enabled.

Fig. S4. Normalized width and height of the 16,234 DENTEX training boxes by permanent FDI class. These distributions describe training geometry; the SpatialShape inference term is a joint quadratic score in log-width and log-height.

Fig. S5. Validation learning curves of controlled base and combined models across the three acquisition domains. Lines show the mean COCO AP at each actual epoch; shaded bands show the sample standard deviation across seeds 0, 1, and 2. All 160 recorded epochs are displayed without smoothing. Pano curves exclude factor inference fusion and anatomical priors. Curves represent online training-validation records; endpoint tables use frozen-checkpoint FP32 replay.

Fig. S6. Internal branch, temperature, and background-loss sensitivity at seed 0. (A) HOOA branches relative to the intact Mobile combined model. (B) Prototype temperature at four prototypes per class, relative to τ = 0.20. (C) NWD and arch-position losses relative to their joint use. (D) Training/inference factor fusion relative to fusion disabled in both phases. Each inference pair uses the same frozen weight within its training state. Positive values mean that the displayed alternative exceeds its specified reference. “—” denotes an incomplete training/replay condition and has no numeric point. The remaining internal families are shown in main Fig. 11.

Fig. S7. Detection and threshold diagnostics for seed-0 controlled base and domain-configured models. Rows show Mobile, Pano, and DSLR. Columns show category-macro-averaged COCO interpolated precision at IoU 0.50 and maxDets = 100; F1; and the fraction of validation images containing repeated raw FDI labels. Categories without validation support are omitted from the precision macro-average. Threshold curves use native top-300 outputs without added NMS and score thresholds 0.05–0.95 in steps of 0.05. Class-agnostic Hungarian localization matching at IoU ≥0.50 is followed by exact FDI comparison. Pano includes the combined prior. Dotted lines indicate score 0.30. These single-seed diagnostics do not measure clinical charting-error rates.

Fig. S8. Within-class prototype cohesion for every FDI slot in the Mobile seed-0 checkpoint. (A) Permanent and (B) primary FDI classes. Cohesion is the mean of the six pairwise cosine similarities among the four normalized prototypes of a class. FDI 18, 28, 38, and 48 have no smartphone training instances and are shown as unavailable; their initialized prototype slots are excluded from learned-evidence interpretation. The bank supplies training auxiliary supervision and is distinct from the fixed Pano center and shape templates.

Fig. S9. Complete Pano FDI outcome matrix and class support. The Factor + Prototype checkpoint includes the joint SpatialShape prior. All 32 permanent classes are shown in clinical FDI order after decoding the native enumeration. The matrix contains 1,861 reference teeth: 1,710 correct identities, 128 wrong-FDI localized matches, and 23 missed teeth. Its 183 unmatched predictions are excluded from the reference-row matrix. The training support totals 16,234 teeth.

Fig. S10. Complete Mobile FDI outcome matrix and class support for the combined 1024-resolution model. All 52 clinical FDI slots are shown. The matrix contains 2,459 reference teeth: 2,134 correct identities, 204 wrong-FDI localized matches, and 121 missed teeth. Its 479 unmatched predictions are excluded from the reference-row matrix. Training support totals 9,837 teeth; FDI 18, 28, 38, and 48 have no training instances. Gray rows indicate absent validation support.

Fig. S11. Complete DSLR FDI outcome matrix and class support for CMFA + DualOpt. All 52 clinical FDI slots are shown. The matrix contains 2,742 reference teeth: 2,617 correct identities, 57 wrong-FDI localized matches, and 68 missed teeth. Its 240 unmatched predictions are excluded from the reference-row matrix. Training support totals 10,760 teeth. Gray rows indicate absent validation support; zero training support is separately visible in the count column.
